ratings_why.fun: Every buff you land pays out again down the vine, and picking whom to climb each turn is a real, readable choice; chains of climbers on climbers get hard to follow late.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: Bloom makes you want a tiny host under a big climber, the reverse of every stack-one-unit tribe, and the tribe grows off other tribes' gains instead of its own.

verdict_why: The core keyword is missing its fall rule and a few cards (Dodder Thread, Lady Hedera, Start of Combat Bloom) don't say what happens; fix the wording, keep the design.

points.text: Climb never says what happens when the host dies or leaves; only the rationale says the climber falls onto the biggest unit next to it. Put that in the keyword, since Old Man's Beard and Birds' Fly South depend on it.
Dodder Thread: does it let go of its friendly host, and does the enemy lose the quarter it takes? Say "steals" and say its own climbers keep copying it.
Lady Hedera climbs your biggest other unit each turn, which may be one of her own climbers, a loop the tribe bans. Add "that isn't climbing her".
Ivy in Flower and Viscum Highbough change sizes at Start of Combat, which can switch Bloom on or off mid-fight. Say Bloom is checked once, at Start of Combat.
Half of half down a chain is hard to work out at a glance. Show each climber's copied stats as a separate leaf number, so the board shows what came from the host.

standouts.why: Mistletoe Clump drains its host as the plant really does, and that drain is what sets up Bloom.
Cousin Dodder hops from enemy to enemy as each one dies: the gatecrasher you end up feeding, in one line.
Ruin Ivy holding up its fragile host with Damage Reduction is the ivy-clad ruin, in play.

weakest.why: Hanger-on is a plain gold unit; the biggest-unit check is the only nod to climbing.
Viscum Highbough is a generic team buff per count; nothing about old blood or oak shows in what it does.
Hop Bine reads fine but is a standard End of Turn buff that any tribe could carry.

flags.note: Re-hosting onto her own climber is not covered.
Whether it leaves its friendly host and whether the stats are stolen is not stated.
Two hosts with the at-least-1 minimum grows well past a Tier 1 seed late.
A huge host dying early can hand five climbers a large share at once.
Full share on a junction under Lady Hedera or a Dodder can stack fast; worth the owner's eye.
